title: unified-rollouts-proactive-shadow-canary-autorollback-enhancement
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes:
- Enhance proactive shadow+canary autorollback: add metric matching, staged probing, and safety gates.
- Metrics and observability: new rollback reasons and per-stage latency/error histograms.
- E2E tests: added stability guards for staged probing.
description:
Motivation: We observed flaky gradual rollouts for some backends where shadow traffic silently masked regressions, and existing auto-rollback triggers lacked staged probing and metric matching for shadow/canary hybrids. This PR improves safety for unified rollouts by implementing proactive staged probing, transparent metric matching for shadow and canary traffic, and stronger safety gates to prevent noisy signals from causing cascading rollbacks.

What this change does:
- Adds a staged probing phase that ramps probes against the candidate variant with low QPS before promoting to higher canary weights.
- Implements transparent metric matching so shadow-only requests are evaluated against the same SLI buckets used for canaries (latency P99, error rate, model-quality eval scores).
- Introduces an aggregate "rollback_reason" taxonomy (latency, error_rate, quality_regression, infra_unhealthy) surfaced to observability and the rollout controller.
- Adds stability guards: minimum sample sizes, debounce windows, and cross-metric confirmation to avoid noisy single-metric rollbacks.
- Updates the rollback engine to allow staged auto-rollback actions (revert to previous variant, reduce weight, or pause) configurable per-rollout policy.
- Adds e2e and unit tests for staged probing, metric matching, and the new rollback flows.
- Docs: rollout API examples and guidance for configuring proactive shadow+canary deployments.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests added for probing scheduler and metric matcher.
- [x] E2E tests for staged probing and rollback flows.
- [x] Observability dashboards updated and alert tests included.
- [x] Docs + API examples added.
- [x] Linear tasks linked: ENG-3241 (design + controller), ENG-3310 (observability).

Testing notes:
- Local unit test suite: all green.
- CI initially failed due to a flakey e2e that assumes timing for probing windows; I adjusted the test to use a deterministic clock and re-ran CI. Full test matrix passed on second run.
- Manual verification on staging: launched a staged shadow->canary rollout against a canary model with injected latency regression; rollout correctly staged probing, flagged quality_regression and auto-rolled back to previous variant with a descriptive rollback_reason.

Rollout policy default: new rollouts opt-in to proactive_staged_probe=false to preserve existing behavior; orgs can opt-in per-rollout with policy: {"proactive_staged_probe": true, "min_sample": 100, "debounce_ms": 300000}.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the probing scheduler (pkg/rollout/probe_scheduler.go), metric matching logic (pkg/rollout/metric_matcher.go), and rollback engine changes (pkg/rollout/rollback_engine.go). Observability changes are minimal code-wise but add important labels and histograms.

review_comments: Ben Rodriguez (reviewer): Overall looks good. A few nits: 1) ensure probe scheduler respects per-customer rate limits when ramping probe QPS, 2) better error strings in metric_matcher for missing histograms.
Aisha Khan (author): Thanks Ben — added customer rate limiter into probe scheduler and improved error messages in metric_matcher (see commit 'Add customer rate limiter and clearer errors').
Liu Zhang (reviewer): We should guard the new histogram labels to avoid cardinality explosion; prefer a finite enum for rollback_reason and a boolean 'stage_probe' label rather than freeform strings.
Aisha Khan (author): Agreed — changed rollback_reason to enum and replaced freeform stage labels with 'stage=probe|canary|baseline'. Updated instrumentation accordingly.

Evan Patel (reviewer): E2E was flaky first run; after switching to deterministic clock, tests are stable in my runs. One question: should we expose the debounce window in the UI? Not necessary for launch but good follow-up (ENG-3419).
Aisha Khan (author): Noted; created follow-up ENG-3419 to evaluate UI surface for debounce/guard tuning.
